case_title: Sushil Sharma v. State of N.C.T. of Delhi
aggravating_circumstances: Possessiveness, motive based on suspicion of infidelity, conspiracy to destroy evidence, brutal murder
mitigating_circumstances: No criminal antecedents, remorse shown by appellant, family circumstances, time spent in death cell
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC and s.120-B rlw s.201 IPC, sentenced to death
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 IPC and s.120-B rlw s.201 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married to the victim, suspected her of having an affair with another person and did not want to make their marriage public. The victim insisted on making the marriage public, leading to a strained relationship. On the night of the incident, the accused killed the victim, likely using a firearm, and then conspired with an accomplice to burn her body in a tandoor at his restaurant. Evidence included blood-stained items, a recovered firearm, and a post-mortem report indicating fatal gunshot wounds. The accused was apprehended after fleeing the scene, and the body was identified as the victim's. The prosecution established a chain of circumstantial evidence pointing to the accused's guilt, including the presence of the accused at the restaurant during the fire and the recovery of items from the crime scene.
